sentences.text: According to prosecution version, the opposite party no.2 has lodged the first information report on 21.06.2022 under Sections 376, 323, 354Ka IPC and Section 7/8 POCSO Act against the applicants and one Iqbal @ Balla, Mahmood and Dilshad, alleging that about three years back, she used to work at the house of co-accused Iqbal @ Balla and for her stay she was provided a room at his house.
After some days, co-accused Iqbal committed rape upon her but due to his influence she could not disclose the incident to any one.
Later, co-accused Iqbal and his brother Mahmood often subjected her to rape.
When daughter of opposite party no.2 used to visit her, the applicants have started keeping evil eye on her and they did obscene acts against her.
When the opposite party no.2/informant opposed, she was assaulted by the accused persons, resultantly, she has sustained injuries.

After about 4-5 months, she managed to run away from the house of co-accused Iqbal @
Balla and started residing with her relative and thereafter, the first information report was lodged.
After investigation police have submitted charge-sheet against accused persons including the applicants.
4. Learned Senior Advocate submitted that the allegations levelled against the applicants are wholly false and there is long and undue delay in lodging of the first information report.
The alleged witnesses, namely, Salman and Abdul Kadir are pocket witness of informant and they have not stated anything about molestation of prosecutrix/informant.
The investigation was not conducted in a free and fair manner.

An SLP No.655 of 2024 was filed by the applicants before the Hon'ble Apex Court and same was withdrawn by vide order dated 16.01.2024 so as to avail remedy as mentioned in judgment dated 08.08.2023, passed in Criminal Appeal No.2342 of 2023 (Iqbal @ Bala and others Vs. State of UP and others), which was filed by co-accused Iqbal @ Balla.

Thereafter,
applicants have filed a discharge application (Paper No.52 Ka) taking several grounds but it was rejected by the trial Court in an arbitrary manner.
The discharge application was rejected mainly on the ground that case is at the stage of defence evidence.
It was submitted that the observations made by Hon'ble Apex Court in order dated 08.08.2023 were not complied with in letter and spirit.

It was submitted that in statement of informant/prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she has stated that at the time of incident, police have reached at the spot and she was medically examined but at that time no complaint was made.
The first information report was lodged after three years of alleged incident.

The alleged school certificate of Class 5th of victim, wherein her date of birth was shown as 28.06.2003, has been procured by the prosecutrix/informant from 'Madarsa' on 17.07.2022 in order to aggravate gravity of the offence.
Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that no case under Section 7/8 POCSO Act is made out.

As per school certificate,
prosecutrix is aged about 18 years, 11 months, 23 days.

5. It is further submitted that co-accused Iqbal @ Balla, after availing remedy before this Court by means of Writ Petition No.8905 of 2022, has approached Hon'ble Apex Court by means of Criminal Appeal No.2342 of 2023.
Hon'ble Apex Court by order dated 08.08.2023 has provided opportunity to him for filing discharge application.

In terms of order dated 08.08.2023, co-accused Iqbal @
Balla has filed discharge application before the trial Court, which was rejected by order dated 28.08.2023.
He has filed a criminal revision against that order and it was dismissed vide order dated 31.05.2024.

Referring to facts of the matter, it was submitted that no prima-facie case is made out against the applicants and that the grounds taken in discharge application have not been considered by the trial Court.

It was submitted that impugned order dated 28.06.2024 is against Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85489379/
2 facts and law and thus, liable to be set aside and the impugned proceedings are also liable to be quashed.

8. In case of Sanjay Kumar Ray (supra), Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:-

3 ''15.

sentences.text: The correct position of law as laid down in Madhu Limaye (supra), thus, is that orders framing charges or refusing discharge are neither interlocutory nor final in nature and are therefore not affected by the bar of Section 397 (2) of CrPC.

That apart, this Court in the abovecited cases has unequivocally acknowledged that the High Court is imbued with inherent jurisdiction to prevent abuse of process or to secure ends of justice having regard to the facts and circumstance of individual cases.
As a caveat it may be stated that the High Court, while exercising its aforestated jurisdiction ought to be circumspect.
The discretion vested in the High Court is to be invoked carefully and judiciously for effective and timely administration of criminal justice system.
This Court, nonetheless, does not recommend a complete hands off approach.
Albeit, there should be interference, may be, in exceptional cases, failing which there is likelihood of serious prejudice to the rights of a citizen.

For example,
when the contents of a complaint or the other purported material on record is a brazen attempt to persecute an innocent person, it becomes imperative upon the Court to prevent the abuse of process of law.
16. Further, it is well settled that the trial court while considering the discharge application is not to act as a mere post office.
The Court has to sift through the evidence in order to find out whether there are sufficient grounds to try the suspect.
The court has to consider the broad probabilities, total effect of evidence and documents produced and the basic infirmities appearing in the case and so on.
[Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal5].

entities.text: Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Likewise, the Court has sufficient discretion to order further investigation in appropriate cases, if need be.''
9.

In case of Haji Iqbal @ Bala (supra), the Apex Court held:
''11.
We take notice of the fact that in the entire FIR there is not a whisper of any allegation of rape or criminal intimidation against the appellant herein.
All that appears on a plain reading of the FIR is that the appellant has been named as the accused No. 2.
The other co-accused persons are directly or indirectly related to the appellant.
The appellant is a Vice Chancellor of the Glocal University.

We may not go into the serious allegations of political bias, etc. levelled by the learned senior counsel appearing for the appellant, but at the same time we should also not overlook the fact that for some reason or the other, the appellant is being targeted.
The appellant has been shown as a history sheeter.

If the FIR does not disclose anything against the appellant and even at the end of the investigation, if nothing incriminating has surfaced against the appellant herein, then the continuation of the criminal proceedings against the appellant herein would be nothing but gross abuse of the process of law.
It appears that so far as the other co-accused are concerned, the investigation has been completed and charge sheet has also been filed.
It further appears that the trial is in progress.

12. We are of the view that in the absence of any particular allegation in the FIR against the appellant herein, the High Court should not have declined to quash the Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85489379/
4 FIR by way of a cryptic order saying that the appellant has criminal antecedents and the FIR prima facie reveals commission of congnizable offences.

sentences.text: The High Court should have first inquired as to what type of allegations have been levelled against the appellant.
By just naming the appellant in the FIR, offence cannot be said to have been committed by him.
If any particular role is attributed or some kind of active participation is alleged in relation to the alleged offence, then it would be a different scenario.
13. There is something more to add to the aforesaid and the same goes to the root of the matter.
We take notice of the fact that for the alleged act of gang rape of 2018, the FIR came to be lodged sometime in the year 2022 i.e. after almost a period of four years.
We do not propose to say anything in regard to delay in lodging the FIR as the trial against the other accused persons is in progress.
The Trial Court on its own will examine this aspect.

It cannot be lost sight of that rape causes the greatest distress and humiliation to the victim but at the same time a false allegation of rape can cause equal distress, humiliation and damage to the accused as well.
The accused must also be protected against the possibility of false implication, particularly where a large number of accused are involved.

It must, further, be borne in mind that the broad principle is that an injured witness was present at the time when the incident happened and that ordinarily such a witness would not tell a lie as to the actual assailants, but there is no presumption or any basis for assuming that the statement of such a witness is always correct or without any embellishment or exaggeration.[See : Raju & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2008) 15 SCC 133].
14.

entities.text: Raju & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2008) 15 SCC 133
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, we would like to observe something important.

Whenever an accused comes before the Court invoking either the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) or extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution to get the FIR or the criminal proceedings quashed essentially on the ground that such proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances the Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely.

We say so because once the complainant decides to proceed against the accused with an ulterior motive for wreaking personal vengeance, etc., then he would ensure that the FIR/complaint is very well drafted with all the necessary pleadings.
The complainant would ensure that the averments made in the FIR/complaint are such that they disclose the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence.

Therefore, it will not be just enough for the Court to look into the averments made in the FIR/complaint alone for the purpose of ascertaining whether the necessary ingredients to constitute the alleged offence are disclosed or not.

In frivolous or vexatious proceedings, the Court owes a duty to look into many other attending circumstances emerging from the record of the case over and above the averments and, if need be, with due care and circumspection try to read in between the lines.

The Court while exercising its jurisdiction under Section 482 of the CrPC or Article 226 of the Constitution need not restrict itself only to the stage of a case but is Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85489379/
5 empowered to take into account the overall circumstances leading to the initiation/registration of the case as well as the materials collected in the course of investigation.

entities.text: Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Take for instance the case on hand.
Multiple FIRs have been registered over a period of time.
It is in the background of such circumstances the registration of multiple FIRs assumes importance, thereby attracting the issue of wreaking vengeance out of private or personal grudge as alleged.
15. In the overall view of the matter, we are convinced that no case is made out to put the appellant herein to trial for the alleged offence.''

10. In case of Beena Singh (supra), the trial court has not adverted to the material accompanying the police report while passing the order on discharge application and it was observed by this court the trial court can not act as merely as post office and in derogation of the observations made by the Apex Court in Sanjay Kumar Rai.

In case of Mohammad Wajid (supra) as well as in case of Moahmood Ali (supra), the proceeding were quashed by the Hon'ble Apex Court by considering peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and it was observed that the proceeding were nothing but abuse of the process of the law.
11. Coming to the facts of the present case, it may be stated that by the impugned order the discharge application of applicants has been rejected.
Instead of availing the remedy of revision, the applicants preferred this application under section 482 CrPC.

Considering law laid down in case of Prabhu Chawla Vs State of Rajasthan 2016 SCC Online SC 905, the jurisdiction under section 482 CrPC is not completely barred against such order but when such an order is challenged under section 482 CrPC, interference can only be made to prevent abuse of the process of court or in any other extra-ordinary situation, which excites Court's jurisdiction.
12.

entities.text: Prabhu Chawla Vs State of Rajasthan 2016 SCC Online SC 905
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant matter it could not be disputed that in the case in question, after framing of charges, the prosecution evidence has already been led and the trial of applicant is at the stage of statement of accused persons under section 313 CrPC.

As per provisions of section 31 of POCSO Act,
a case under POCSO Act has to be tried in accordance with the procedure prescribed for Session trial cases.
A question arises whether after charges have been framed and prosecution evidence has been led, at that stage an application for discharge would be maintainable?.

In case of Ratilal Bhanji Mithani (supra), it was observed that once charge is framed in a warrant case, the Magistrate has no power to discharge the accused and he can either acquit or convict the accused.

In case of Bharat Parikh (supra), the Apex Court held:
''15.

Of the two propositions raised in this appeal, the first proposition has been completely answered in Debendra Nath Padhi's case (supra) regarding the trial court's power to recall its order framing charge against an accused.

Having regard to the language of Sections 207 and 227 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, while framing charges the trial court can only look into the materials produced by the prosecution while giving an opportunity to the accused to show that the said materials were insufficient for the purpose of framing charge.

The decision in Satish Mehra's case (supra) having been overruled in Debendra Nath Padhi's case (supra)
Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85489379/

entities.text: Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 6 the contention of Mr. Desai that the Magistrate should have re-opened the matter on the basis of the documents produced by the prosecution at the instance of the accused, is no longer res-integra.

The question of discharge by the learned Magistrate after framing of charge does not, therefore, arise, notwithstanding the submissions advanced with regard to denial of natural justice and a fair and speedy trial as contemplated under Article 21 of the Constitution, which have no application whatsoever to the facts of this case.

16. With regard to the second proposition regarding the High Court's powers to look into materials produced on behalf of or at the instance of the accused for the purpose of invoking its powers under Section 482 of the Code for quashing the charges framed, it has to be kept in mind that after the stage of framing charge evidence has to be led on behalf of the prosecution to prove the charge if an accused pleads not guilty to the charge and/or charges and claims to be tried.

It is only in the exceptional circumstances enumerated in State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Suppl.(1) SCC 335, that a criminal proceeding may be quashed to secure the ends of justice, but such a stage will come only after evidence is led, particularly when the prosecution had produced sufficient material for charges to be framed.

entities.text: State of Haryana vs. Bhajan Lal 1992 Suppl.(1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As observed in Debendra Nath Padhi's case (supra) at the stage of framing charge roving and fishing inquiry is impermissible and a mini trial cannot be conducted at such stage.
At the stage of framing of charge the submissions on behalf of the accused has to be confined to the material produced by the investigating agency.

The accused will get an opportunity to prove the documents subsequently produced by the prosecution on the order of the Court, but the same cannot be relied upon to re-open the proceedings once charge has been framed or for invocation of the High Court's powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.''
13. Though that pronouncement relates to Magistrate trial cases but similar analogy may also be drawn in respect of Session trial case.

It would be pertinent to mention that in procedure of Session trial under chapter XVIII CrPC after stage of section 227/228 CrPC is over and after framing of charges prosecution evidence has been led, there is no provision of discharge.
In procedure prescribed for Session trial cases, there is no such provision like section section 246 CrPC, which is prescribed for warrant trial cases.
None of the aforesaid case law lays down any such preposition that in a Session trial case an application of discharge can be entertained after prosecution evidence is over.
Thus, at the stage i.e. where prosecution evidence has already been led, the application of applicants for discharge can not be held maintainable.

It appears that the applicants / accused did not bring stage of trial in to notice of the Hon'ble Apex Court in aforesaid SLP, whereby the applicants were provided liberty to file discharge application.

However, section 232 CrPC provides in Session Trial case, after taking prosecution evidence, examining the accused and hearing the prosecution and the defence on the point, the Judge considers that there is no evidence that the accused committed the offence, the Judge shall record an order of acquittal.
14. There is yet another angle in the matter.
The order by which charges were framed against the applicants has not been challenged.

If after framing of charges, the application seeking discharge is Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85489379/
7 filed and rejected, as happened in the present case, and applicants choose to challenge the order passed on discharge application, the order by which charges were framed, has also to be impugned but in the instant case the order of framing of charges is not being challenged.

entities.text: Javed And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. Though, in view of aforesaid position of law the discharge application was not maintainable at the stage, where prosecution evidence has already been led, however, even on merits it may be stated that in her statement, the informant has inter-alia made allegations that she used to work at the house of co-accused Iqbal @ Balla and reside there in a room provided to her.
She has alleged that co-accused Iqbal committed rape upon her and that when her daughter used to visit her, the applicants had an evil eye on her and they did obscene acts (cherchar) with her.

In her statement under section 164 CrPC, daughter of informant has stated that she used to visit her mother and that applicants had caught her by hands and took her inside the room and they touched chest, shoulder and cheeks.
She is a minor girl.

Though, as stated earlier there is long delay in lodging of the first information report and the applicants are brothers but considering all relevant facts, particularly the stage of trial, as prosecution evidence has already been led, it could not be said that impugned order is suffering from any such patent illegality or perversity or abuse of process of court, so as to require any interference by this court by invoking provisions of section 482 CrPC..
The application under section 482 CrPC lacks merit and thus, liable to be dismissed.
16. The application under section 482 CrPC is dismissed.

The accused must also be protected against the possibility of false implication, particularly where a large number of accused are involved.
It must, further, be borne in mind that the broad principle is that an injured witness was present at the time when the incident happened and that ordinarily such a witness would not tell a lie as to the actual assailants, but there is no presumption or any basis for assuming that the statement of such a witness is always correct or without any embellishment or exaggeration.[See : Raju & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2008) 15 SCC 133].
14.
Whenever an accused comes before the Court invoking either the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) or extraordinary jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution to get the FIR or the criminal proceedings quashed essentially on the ground that such proceedings are manifestly frivolous or vexatious or instituted with the ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance, then in such circumstances the Court owes a duty to look into the FIR with care and a little more closely.
Considering law laid down in case of Prabhu Chawla Vs State of Rajasthan 2016 SCC Online SC 905, the jurisdiction under section 482 CrPC is not completely barred against such order but when such an order is challenged under section 482 CrPC, interference can only be made to prevent abuse of the process of court or in any other extra-ordinary situation, which excites Court's jurisdiction.
12.
In the instant matter it could not be disputed that in the case in question, after framing of charges, the prosecution evidence has already been led and the trial of applicant is at the stage of statement of accused persons under section 313 CrPC.
Having regard to the language of Sections 207 and 227 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, while framing charges the trial court can only look into the materials produced by the prosecution while giving an opportunity to the accused to show that the said materials were insufficient for the purpose of framing charge.
At the stage of framing of charge the submissions on behalf of the accused has to be confined to the material produced by the investigating agency.
Though, as stated earlier there is long delay in lodging of the first information report and the applicants are brothers but considering all relevant facts, particularly the stage of trial, as prosecution evidence has already been led, it could not be said that impugned order is suffering from any such patent illegality or perversity or abuse of process of court, so as to require any interference by this court by invoking provisions of section 482 CrPC..
